\begin{table*}[t]
\centering
\scriptsize
\caption{Comparison with the two closest evaluation-under-shift papers. Tags in the last column: [KNOWN] prior art reused; [ADAPTED] a known ingredient transposed to the missing-feature setting; [UNVERIFIED novelty] not found in the two papers read, but no forward-citation search was done.}
\label{tab:comparison}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.14\textwidth} p{0.26\textwidth} p{0.26\textwidth} p{0.29\textwidth}}
\toprule
Aspect & \citet{subbaswamy2021evaluating} & \citet{guerdan2024predictive} & This paper \\
\midrule
Observed information &
One i.i.d.\ test sample with $X,Y$ fully observed; analyst splits variables into immutable $Z$, mutable $W$, dependent $V$; the shift replaces $P(W\mid Z)$ by $Q(W\mid Z)$ with $P(Z)$ and $P(V\mid W,Z)$ fixed (Sec.~2.1). &
Selective labels: $Y$ observed only when the status-quo decision $D^{\pi_0}=1$; data $(X,T^{\pi},D^{\pi_0},Y)$ from the status-quo policy; proposed policy $\pi$ known (Sec.~3). &
[ADAPTED] Complete cases with labels ($\theta_c$) plus unlabelled incomplete tuples $\omega(r,o)=P(R=r,X_r=o)$ (setting~C); less in B/D; full-data law only in oracle~A. Their $(W,Z)$-shift with $W=R$, $Z=(X,Y)$, but conditioned on what is observable under masking. \\
\midrule
Comparison estimand &
Worst-case risk $R_{\alpha,0}$ of \emph{one} fixed model: expected loss on the worst $(1-\alpha)$-subsample (Eq.~1--2); two models are compared by their separate worst-case curves (Fig.~4a). &
Regret $m^*(\pi)-m^*(\pi_0)$; Def.~4.1 baseline interval subtracts separate bounds, Def.~4.2 $\delta$-regret optimises the difference jointly over $\mathcal{V}(p)$; Thm.~4.3 quantifies the gain. &
[KNOWN] Risk difference $\Delta_{\mathrm{nat}}=\sum_{c,r}p(c,r)D(c,r)$ of two fixed predictors under the same unknown natural-mask law, optimised jointly over $p$ by two LPs; the cancellation is an instance of their Def.~4.2 and is not claimed as new. \\
\midrule
Sensitivity / uncertainty model &
One-sided likelihood-ratio ball on $P(W\mid Z)$: $dQ/dP\le 1/(1-\alpha)$ a.e.\ (App.\ Eq.~11--12; $D_\infty$ ball, Remark~3); $Q\ll P$ by construction; $\alpha$ user-chosen. &
Pointwise bounding functions $\underline{\tau}(x)\le\mathbb{E}[Y(1)\mid D=0,X=x]\le\overline{\tau}(x)$ (Asm.~5.1), implied by MSM/Rosenbaum/IV/proximal; e.g.\ MSM gives $\Lambda^{-1}\mu_1\le\mu_0\le\Lambda\mu_1$ (Lemma~B.4); yields the box $\mathcal{V}(p;\tau)$. &
[ADAPTED] Pattern-mixture bounded ratio $\lambda_r/\Gamma\le P(C=c\mid R=r)/v_c\le\lambda_r\Gamma$ relative to the complete-case law, free scale $\lambda_r$ per mask, absolute continuity ($\mathcal{M}_{cc}(\Gamma)$, two-sided); $\Gamma$ analyst-chosen, not estimable. \\
\midrule
Sharpness claim &
$R_{\alpha,0}$ is point-identified; the sup in Eq.~1 equals the conditional-quantile (CVaR-type) dual, Eq.~3--4; no partial-identification sharpness question arises. &
Lemma~5.2 bounds are sharp given $\tau$ (App.~B.6.1); Thm.~5.3: $\mathcal{V}(p;\tau)$ is minimal given $\tau$; App.~B.1/B.6.2 state this does \emph{not} guarantee the tightest regret interval under the causal assumption itself. &
[UNVERIFIED novelty] LP interval is the closure of the identified set of $\Delta_{\mathrm{nat}}$ under the stated assumptions when a valid law exists; attained vs closure-only endpoints separated by one extra LP; exact observable threshold $\Gamma_{\min}(o)$ in closed form (C, D) with $\Gamma_{\min}(o)\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{true}}$. \\
\midrule
Sampling uncertainty &
Cross-fitted debiased estimator (Alg.~1, Eq.~5); Thm.~1: $\sqrt{N}$-consistent and asymptotically normal; Wald CIs from Eq.~7; variance scales as $1/(1-\alpha)^2$; discrete $W$ needs noise augmentation (Remark~6). &
Cross-fitted plug-in (Alg.~1; Thm.~6.1: error inherits nuisance rates $+O_P(n^{-1/2})$); doubly robust variant for the MSM (Eq.~2, App.~C); 95\% bootstrap CIs around interval endpoints in experiments. &
[ADAPTED] Conservative outer interval: Hoeffding/Bonferroni box on the observable multinomial, relaxed LP; on one event it covers the identified interval for all $\Gamma$ simultaneously and covers $\Delta_{\mathrm{nat}}$ for $\Gamma\ge\Gamma_{\mathrm{true}}$; it does not validate $\Gamma$; not sharp, no width analysis. \\
\midrule
Not claimed here &
Outside their scope: a bound on the \emph{difference} between two models under a common shift; a two-sided ratio; partially observed features. &
Outside their scope: feature masks; constraints from unlabelled incomplete observations; attained-vs-closure endpoint distinction. &
[KNOWN] LP bounds, the direct-difference bound, joint-versus-separate cancellation, bounded-ratio sensitivity models and tipping-point $\Gamma^*$ summaries are prior art; no $\sqrt{n}$ or doubly robust inference, no data-based validation of $\Gamma$, no forward-citation novelty check. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table*}
row_notes: Observed information: relative to Subbaswamy et al. the assumption that all of (X,Y) is observed in the test sample is dropped (labels only on complete cases, features only partly observed), and relative to Guerdan et al. the missing quantity is the feature vector and label jointly rather than the outcome alone; what survives is the W=R, Z=(X,Y) reading of the shift and the selective-labels style information structure. Comparison estimand: relative to Subbaswamy et al. the estimand changes from one model's worst-case risk to a difference of two fixed predictors, and relative to Guerdan et al. only the object changes (predictor losses under masks instead of policy regret under selective labels); the conclusion that bounding the difference jointly cancels shared uncertainty is theirs and survives unchanged. Sensitivity/uncertainty model: relative to Subbaswamy et al. the one-sided ratio bound dQ/dP <= 1/(1-alpha) is replaced by a two-sided ratio with a free per-mask scale, and relative to Guerdan et al. the bounded quantity is the pattern-mixture ratio P(C|R=r)/v_c rather than the outcome regression E[Y(1)|D=0,X]; the bounded-likelihood-ratio idea (MSM/Rosenbaum-type) survives. Sharpness claim: Subbaswamy et al. have a point-identified target so no sharpness question arises; relative to Guerdan et al., whose minimality is stated for the uncertainty set given tau and explicitly not for the interval under the causal assumption itself, this paper's claim is for the identified set under its own stated sensitivity model, with the attainment-versus-closure distinction and Gamma_min(o) formula not found in either paper but not checked against the wider literature. Sampling uncertainty: both prior papers assume nuisance-function estimation and give asymptotic (sqrt N / bootstrap) intervals, whereas this paper assumes a finite multinomial and gives a non-asymptotic, conservative outer box valid simultaneously in Gamma; the common conclusion that the sensitivity parameter (alpha, Lambda, Gamma) is user-chosen and not validated by the data survives in all three. Not claimed here: no assumption changes; this row records that the LP, the direct-difference bound, the cancellation argument and Gamma* are inherited, and that efficient inference (which both prior papers provide in their settings) is absent here.
novelty_assessment: Against the two papers actually read, the combination that is not present in either is: a risk-difference bound for two fixed predictors under an unknown, possibly label-dependent missing-feature policy, with a two-sided pattern-mixture ratio model relative to the complete-case law, information from unlabelled incomplete observations, and an explicit attained-versus-closure endpoint distinction plus a closed-form observable threshold Gamma_min(o). Subbaswamy et al. (2021) already evaluate a fixed model under a shift of P(test order | demographics, disease status) with a one-sided ratio bound and report two models' worst-case risks separately; Guerdan et al. (2024) already bound a performance difference jointly and note that their minimality is relative to the bounding functions, not to the causal assumption, so neither the difference-bounding idea nor the sharpness caveat is new here. Whether the specific ingredients tagged [UNVERIFIED novelty] (closure characterisation with attainment check, Gamma_min(o) formula, use of the unlabelled observed law as linear constraints in a Gamma-box) appear elsewhere is UNVERIFIED: no forward-citation search of Subbaswamy 2021 or Guerdan 2024 and no search of the 2025-2026 missing-data or partial-identification literature was performed in this pass. The linear-programming machinery and the bounded-ratio sensitivity model are standard and should be described as reused.
caveats: (1) No WebFetch summariser was used; both papers were read from locally text-extracted arXiv/ar5iv HTML, and the published PMLR PDFs were only grep-checked (crude extraction) to confirm the key sentences match. (2) Guerdan et al.: Sections 1-2 and 9 and Appendices A, C, D, E were not read (only grepped); the doubly robust 'second-order error' claim is taken from the Sec. 6.2 sentence pointing to App. C, which I did not read. (3) Subbaswamy et al.: the explicit one-sided bound q(W|Z)/p(W|Z) <= 1/(1-alpha) appears in the Appendix (Eq. 11-12); the main text states it only as a D_infinity divergence ball (Remark 3). Their Fig. 4a compares two models on their respective worst-case subsamples, and a 'comparing to baseline standards' use case evaluates qSOFA on the classical model's worst subsamples; neither is a bound on a difference under a common shift, but the second is a same-subsample comparison and should not be described as entirely absent. Remark 6 (discrete W requires noise augmentation) is relevant because W=R is discrete in this paper's reading. (4) The 'this paper' column restates the manuscript as written (Problem Setup, Identification, Sampling Uncertainty sections); the correctness of those claims was not independently checked, and the experiments/appendices were not read. (5) The table uses no custom macros (\Mcc, \Dnat written out) so it compiles independently of the manuscript preamble; it needs booktabs and natbib-style \citet; with \scriptsize in table* it should fit one page, but line-count was not compiled. (6) Tags are one per cell; the 'Observed information' cell is tagged [ADAPTED] although the unlabelled-observed-law constraint inside it is the ingredient whose novelty is unverified. (7) No forward-citation or 2025-2026 preprint search was done; the novelty statements are limited to the two papers read.
